issues.body: The revision still adds a measurement table containing corpus opcode totals and percentages, per-package opcode deltas, synthetic-chain deltas, and wall-clock compile timings. The companion new research record contains the same classes of hard-coded measurements throughout §§6–7. Repository policy explicitly prohibits hard-coded performance numbers in Markdown and says work-box timings are non-canonical; labeling these figures “non-canonical” does not remove that prohibition. This is materially the same major finding as round 1.
issues.fix_hint: Move raw opcode counts, percentages, package deltas, fixture results, test-run measurements, and wall-clock timings into the repository’s approved generated/result artifact mechanism. Link that artifact from both research records and retain only qualitative, evidence-scoped conclusions in Markdown.
issues.title: Hard-coded performance measurements remain in Markdown

verdict.summary: Round 2 is improving: the unsupported universal “never regresses” language was replaced with evidence-bounded wording, and the duplicated issue-body paragraph was removed. One prior major blocker remains. Both changed Markdown files still embed extensive benchmark results and work-box timings—opcode totals, percentages, package-level deltas, synthetic-fixture measurements, test counts, and compile timings—even though the repository contract prohibits hard-coded performance numbers in Markdown and treats work-box timings as non-canonical. Calling the measurements non-canonical does not satisfy that policy. Move the raw measurements to an approved generated/result artifact and keep the research Markdown qualitative, with links to the artifact.
